source_candidate.candidate: BEP 44 immutable DHT item lookup as a content-addressed alternative for exact Git commit object discovery

primary_sources.title: BEP 44 - Storing arbitrary data in the DHT
verified_points: For immutable items, the DHT target is the SHA-1 hash of the stored value's flattened bencoded representation.
The v field may be any bencoded type; when its key is calculated, the flattened bencoded form is hashed.
An immutable get request supplies target as the SHA-1 hash of the item, and a returned v must hash to that target.
The bencoded representation of v may be rejected above 1000 bytes, so arbitrary Git-object payload size is not generally guaranteed to fit.

Without re-announcement, stored items may expire in about two hours; therefore durable passive availability requires independently pre-existing residency/replication and cannot be inferred from the key derivation alone.

primary_sources.title: Git core data model
primary_sources.version: 2.55.0 documentation; gitdatamodel content last changed in 2.53.0
verified_points: A Git object ID is a cryptographic hash of the object's type and contents.
Commit objects are a distinct Git object type with structured commit contents.

primary_sources.title: Git Internals - Git Objects
verified_points: Git forms an object hash preimage from a type header, a space, the content byte length, a NUL byte, and the object content, then computes SHA-1 for traditional SHA-1 object IDs.
The same storage rule applies to commit objects, with the header beginning with commit rather than blob.

verified_claims.claim: BEP 44 immutable-item target derivation is not the same serialization as Git commit object-ID derivation.
verified_claims.reason: BEP 44 hashes the flattened bencoded representation of v. Git SHA-1 object IDs hash a Git object preimage consisting of type/size header plus NUL plus content. These are distinct protocol serializations.

verified_claims.claim: Placing canonical Git commit bytes inside a BEP 44 immutable v does not directly make the BEP 44 target equal that Git commit's SHA-1 object ID.
verified_claims.reason: If v is a bencoded string carrying Git bytes, BEP 44 hashes the bencoded string including its length-prefix serialization, while Git hashes the Git object header and content. The protocol therefore provides no direct identity-preserving mapping from the Git SHA-1 to the BEP 44 immutable target. Equal 20-byte digests would require an independently established hash collision/second-preimage relation or an external mapping; none is established here.

verified_claims.claim: BEP 44 passive get can only retrieve an item already resident under its BEP 44 target and does not itself publish the target value.
verified_claims.reason: BEP 44 separates get from put, and its expiration rules require re-announcement for persistence. This slice performed no put/publication/re-announcement and established no independently pre-existing target residency.

scope_limits: No live UDP DHT query, put, publication, or re-announcement was executed; this is a primary-source protocol verification only.

The canonical bytes and byte length of Git commit 573f2f0a00718109e2cd2fc1c1c9bf2f5a0404de were not reconstructed in this slice; therefore the BEP 44 <=1000-byte storage bound is recorded as a generic protocol constraint, not claimed to reject this exact commit by size.
No BEP 44 immutable item independently resident at any key corresponding to the target Git object was established.
No currently exposed scheduled-Chat tool surface for issuing BEP 44 UDP DHT get requests was demonstrated; any external DHT client/executor remains unresolved for Phase-1 parity.
The BEP specifies a decentralized protocol, not a hosted public lookup service with a guaranteed zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota contract; no quota-bearing service was used in this verification.
This result does not establish full scheduled-Chat parity or Phase-1 closure.

phase1_assessment.reason: Official BEP 44 semantics hash the flattened bencoded v, whereas a Git commit SHA-1 hashes Git's type/size/NUL object preimage plus commit contents. BEP 44 therefore does not directly preserve the Git commit object ID when storing Git bytes as v. Pre-existing DHT residency and an exposed zero-quota Chat-native live lookup route are also unproven.
